data.title: CodeArena: A Collective Evaluation Platform for LLM Code Generation

form.note: CodeArena is a ready-to-use online evaluation platform that users access directly; its APIs and Python library are supporting interfaces.
form.evidence: CodeArena is an online code evaluation platform built upon an open-source OJ framework DMOJ

activity.note: The platform evaluates code produced by LLMs for programming problems, so its supported coding activity is code generation.
activity.evidence: CodeArena is an online evaluation framework tailored for LLM code generation.

data.title: Enhancing LLM Code Generation: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Collaboration and Runtime Debugging for Improved Accuracy, Reliability, and Latency

form.note: This is a research framework that coordinates analyst, coder, tester, and debugger agents in a multi-step coding workflow, rather than a ready-to-use product.
form.evidence: The framework implements a sequential flow in which the code is first generated using the ACT (analyst, coder, and tester agents) collaboration system.

activity.note: The framework primarily supports generating code from task requirements, with testing and debugging used to refine the generated output.
activity.evidence: we implement a framework that combines the two prominent post-training strategies discussed above—multi-agent collaboration as a process-oriented pipeline to generate the code and runtime execution information-based debugging

data.title: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable

form.note: PlayCoder is presented as a research multi-agent framework for generating and refining GUI application code, rather than as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: we propose PlayCoder, a novel multi-agent framework that leverages two specialized agents

activity.note: Its main supported activity is generating repository-aware GUI application code, with testing and repair used iteratively to improve generated code.
activity.evidence: a multi-agent framework that integrates repository-aware code generation, automated GUI behavioral testing, and iterative program repair

data.title: Paper2Code: Automating Code Generation from Scientific Papers in Machine Learning

form.note: PaperCoder is presented as a research multi-agent system that coordinates planning, analysis, and code generation to produce repositories from papers, rather than as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: we introduce PaperCoder, a multi-agent LLM framework that transforms machine learning papers into operational code repositories

activity.note: Its central purpose is generating complete, repository-level code implementations from scientific papers.
activity.evidence: The goal of our repository-level code generation task is to automatically produce a repository that faithfully implements methods and experiments described in machine learning papers

data.title: Embarrassingly Simple Self-Distillation Improves Code Generation

form.note: SSD is presented as a proposed self-distillation procedure, not as a ready-to-use product; the repository link does not change the paper’s main contribution.
form.evidence: sample solutions from the base model with specified temperature and truncation, then fine-tune on those raw, unverified samples via standard cross-entropy loss

activity.note: The method is evaluated as a way to improve code generation, including on competitive-programming problems.
activity.evidence: SSD improves code generation models’ performance

data.title: StepCoder: Improve Code Generation with Reinforcement Learning from Compiler Feedback

form.note: StepCoder is presented as a proposed reinforcement-learning training framework and method, not as a ready-to-use product or released model.
form.evidence: We introduce StepCoder, a novelty training method via RL, including CCCS and FGO.

activity.note: The method supports generating code from human requirements; its code-completion subtasks are part of the training curriculum for code generation.
activity.evidence: StepCoder, a novel RL framework for code generation

data.title: Think Anywhere in Code Generation

form.note: THINK-ANYWHERE is presented as a reasoning mechanism and training approach for LLMs, not as a ready-to-use product or released model.
form.evidence: we propose THINK-ANYWHERE, a novel reasoning mechanism of LLMs for code generation

activity.note: The mechanism supports producing code from coding requirements, with reasoning invoked during generation.
activity.evidence: enables LLMs to invoke thinking on-demand at any token position during code generation

data.title: GLLM: Self-Corrective G-Code Generation using Large Language Models with User Feedback

form.note: GLLM is presented as a directly usable web application for entering machining tasks and generating G-code.
form.evidence: We developed a user-friendly web interface using Streamlit

activity.note: GLLM translates natural-language machining instructions into executable G-code, so its main supported activity is code generation.
activity.evidence: automatically generate G-code from natural language instructions

data.title: WebVIA: A Web-based Vision-Language Agentic Framework for Interactive and Verifiable UI-to-Code Generation

form.note: WebVIA is presented as a research agentic system that explores webpages, generates code, and validates interactions, rather than as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: we propose WebVIA, the first agentic framework for interactive UI-to-Code generation and validation

activity.note: Its primary coding activity is generating executable, interactive front-end code from UI screenshots and interaction traces.
activity.evidence: the UI2Code model generates executable front-end HTML/CSS/JavaScript code

data.title: Teaching LLMs a Low-Resource Language: Enhancing Code Completion in Pharo

form.note: The solution consists of language models specialized for Pharo, rather than a directly operated product or an integrated library.
form.evidence: we fine-tune these models on a curated Pharo dataset

activity.note: The models are specialized and evaluated primarily to predict missing code in partially written Pharo programs.
activity.evidence: Our goal is, however, in-IDE code completion

data.title: CodeGen: An Open Large Language Model for Code with Multi-Turn Program Synthesis

form.note: CODEGEN is presented as a released family of trained autoregressive language models, so the best-fitting form is Model.
form.evidence: we train and release a family of large language models up to 16.1B parameters, called CODEGEN

activity.note: The models support generating new programs from natural-language specifications, including through multi-turn program synthesis.
activity.evidence: program synthesis strives to generate a computer program as a solution to a given problem specification, expressed with input-output examples or natural language descriptions.

data.title: PanGu-Coder2: Boosting Large Language Models for Code with Ranking Feedback

form.note: PanGu-Coder2 is presented as a trained code language model and the paper’s main model contribution, rather than as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: We present PanGu-Coder2, a model that improves nearly 30% over its base model

activity.note: The model supports generating code from programming problem descriptions; this is the paper’s emphasized and evaluated activity.
activity.evidence: boost pre-trained large language models for code generation

data.title: ScreenCoder: Advancing Visual-to-Code Generation for Front-End Automation via Modular Multimodal Agents

form.note: ScreenCoder is presented as a research framework of specialized agents for grounding, planning, and generating UI code, rather than as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: we propose ScreenCoder, a modular multi-agent framework that decomposes the UI-to-code task into three interpretable stages: grounding, planning, and generation.

activity.note: It supports generating front-end code from UI screenshots or design sketches, which is its central evaluated task.
activity.evidence: ScreenCoder accurately transforms website screenshots and design sketches into pixel-perfect front-end code.

data.title: Efficient Code Embeddings from Code Generation Models

form.note: The contribution is a family of trained code-embedding models, presented and evaluated as the solution.
form.evidence: We have introduced `jina-code-embeddings`, a family of code embedding models with 0.5B and 1.5B parameters.

activity.note: The models primarily support code retrieval, an activity not listed among the allowed categories, so the closest value is Other.
activity.evidence: `jina-code-embeddings` is a novel code embedding model suite designed to retrieve code from natural language queries

data.title: cAST: Enhancing Code Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Structural Chunking via Abstract Syntax Tree

form.note: CAST is presented as an AST-based chunking strategy, with released code, rather than as a ready-to-use product.
form.evidence: we present CAST as a simple and effective chunking strategy for retrieval-augmented code generation.

activity.note: CAST supports retrieval-augmented code generation; the paper evaluates it across several generation tasks, so code generation is the best fit.
activity.evidence: Extensive experiments show that CAST improves performance across a range of code generation tasks.

data.title: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation

form.note: ArtifactsBench is presented primarily as a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts; the evaluation harness is an accompanying artifact.
form.evidence: We introduce ArtifactsBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts.

activity.note: The benchmark evaluates models’ ability to generate executable visual artifacts from instructions, so the supported activity is code generation.
activity.evidence: transform multimodal instructions—spanning text, images, and interaction logic—into high-quality, executable interactive visual artifacts

data.title: LeetCodeDataset: A Temporal Dataset for Robust Evaluation and Efficient Training of Code LLMs

form.note: LeetCodeDataset is presented as a curated benchmark and training dataset for code-generation models, rather than as a directly operated coding product.
form.evidence: We introduce LeetCodeDataset, a high-quality benchmark for evaluating and training code-generation models

activity.note: The dataset supports code generation through evaluation and training; code generation is the activity explicitly emphasized in the text.
activity.evidence: This dataset can also support RL training by leveraging test cases as verifiers, making it a self-contained testbed for LLM development in code generation.

data.title: ReLook: Vision-Grounded RL with a Multimodal LLM Critic for Agentic Web Coding

form.note: ReLook is presented as a research agentic system that iteratively generates and refines front-end code by invoking a multimodal critic, not as a ready-to-use product.
form.evidence: We present ReLook, an agentic, vision-grounded reinforcement learning framework that empowers an agent to close a robust generate–diagnose–refine loop by invoking a multimodal LLM (MLLM) as a tool.

activity.note: Its primary supported activity is generating front-end code from user requests, with visual feedback used to refine the generated output.
activity.evidence: The task of front-end code generation is to produce a code snippet c, consisting of SVG, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, that correctly implements a user’s intent specified in a natural language question q.

data.title: Verus-SpecGym: An Agentic Environment for Evaluating Specification Autoformalization

form.note: VERUS-SPECGYM is an evaluation environment and benchmark infrastructure for measuring agents’ specification autoformalization, rather than a coding product or the agent itself.
form.evidence: VERUS-SPECGYM, an agentic environment for evaluating specification autoformalization

activity.note: The environment supports translating informal programming intent into formal specifications. This specialized activity is not one of the listed code-production or code-maintenance categories, so Other is the closest fit.
activity.evidence: translating informal programming intent into faithful formal specifications

data.title: BigCodeArena: Unveiling More Reliable Human Preferences in Code Generation via Execution

form.note: BIGCODEARENA is a ready-to-use web platform that people use directly to compare and evaluate generated code.
form.evidence: we introduce BIGCODEARENA, a new open human evaluation platform for code generation

activity.note: The platform supports code generation by enabling users to evaluate LLM-generated code; code generation is the activity emphasized throughout the paper.
activity.evidence: BIGCODEARENA, a new platform for human-in-the-loop evaluation of code generation

data.title: Agents4PLC: Automating Closed-loop PLC Code Generation and Verification in Industrial Control Systems using LLM-based Agents

form.note: Agents4PLC is presented as a research multi-agent framework, rather than as a directly operated product; it coordinates agents to generate and verify PLC code.
form.evidence: We propose Agents4PLC, an LLM-based multi-agent framework for automating the generation and verification process of ST code.

activity.note: Its primary supported activity is generating PLC code from user requirements, with validation and debugging included in the workflow.
activity.evidence: The Coding Agent generates ST code accordingly to the received plans

data.title: LongCodeZip: Compress Long Context for Code Language Models

form.note: LongCodeZip is presented as a proposed, training-free compression approach, not as a directly operated product or an integrated library. The paper describes its compression procedure as the contribution.
form.evidence: we introduce LongCodeZip, a training-free, model-agnostic, and plug-and-play context compression framework for code LLMs

activity.note: The approach supports several downstream tasks, but code completion is a central evaluated use case and receives focused analysis in the paper.
activity.evidence: LongCodeZip consistently achieves the highest ES scores across all compression ratios, demonstrating its strong ability to identify and retain the most relevant context for code completion.

data.title: GPIoT: Tailoring Small Language Models for IoT Program Synthesis and Development

form.note: GPIoT is presented as a ready-to-use system for IoT application development, deployed locally for users to generate programs; the text does not identify an IDE plugin, API, or command-line interface.
form.evidence: We propose GPIoT, a code generation system tailored for IoT application development

activity.note: Its emphasized function is generating new IoT-specific programs from user requirements, with code and documentation.
activity.evidence: GPIoT can generate code adopting more IoT-specialized algorithms

data.title: SuperCoder: Assembly Program Superoptimization with Large Language Models

form.note: SuperCoder is presented as a reinforcement-learning fine-tuned language model, not as a directly operated product or reusable software package.
form.evidence: the fine-tuned model SuperCoder attains 95.0% correctness and 1.46× average speedup

activity.note: It improves the performance of existing assembly while preserving behavior. Of the allowed activities, refactoring and restructuring is the closest fit because it includes performance improvement.
activity.evidence: Superoptimization is the task of transforming a program into a faster one while preserving its input–output behavior.

data.title: Nanbeige4.1-3B: A Small General Model that Reasons, Aligns, and Acts

form.note: Nanbeige4.1-3B is presented as an open-source trained language model, with its checkpoint made available; it is not described as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: The model checkpoint is available at `https://huggingface.co/Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.1-3B`

activity.note: The model explicitly supports code generation, and the paper emphasizes generating solutions to programming problems.
activity.evidence: For code generation, we design complexity-aware rewards in Reinforcement Learning, optimizing both correctness and efficiency.

data.title: AST-T5: Structure-Aware Pretraining for Code Generation and Understanding

form.note: AST-T5 is presented as a pretrained code language model, not as a directly operated product or reusable software package.
form.evidence: AST-T5 is a language model aimed at automated generation, transpilation, and understanding of code.

activity.note: The model supports generation, transpilation, and understanding; code generation is the closest primary activity, emphasized in the title and evaluations.
activity.evidence: We introduce AST-T5, a novel pretraining paradigm that leverages the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) for enhanced code generation, transpilation, and understanding.

data.title: SALLM: Security Assessment of Generated Code

form.note: Sallm is presented as a benchmarking framework with a security-focused prompt dataset, assessment environment, and evaluation metrics, rather than as a directly operated coding product.
form.evidence: a framework to benchmark LLMs’ abilities to generate secure code systematically

activity.note: The framework evaluates models’ ability to generate code that is both functionally correct and secure; code generation is its supported activity, while security assessment is how it evaluates the outputs.
activity.evidence: measure to what extent an LLM is capable of generating secure code

data.title: Lean Refactor: Multi-Objective Controllable Proof Optimization via Agentic Strategy Search

form.note: Lean Refactor is presented as a research framework whose agent plans and executes refactoring steps with compiler feedback, not as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: a retrieval-augmented agentic framework

activity.note: It rewrites existing Lean proofs to improve their structure and concision while preserving correctness, so refactoring and restructuring is the best fit.
activity.evidence: refactoring of Lean proofs

data.title: On the Use of Agentic Coding: An Empirical Study of Pull Requests on GitHub

form.note: Claude Code is presented as a ready-to-use coding product operated through a command-line interface, rather than as a research-only agent system.
form.evidence: Fig. 1 illustrates a command-line interaction in which Claude Code performs a refactoring task.

activity.note: Claude Code supports a broad range of coding tasks, including generation, modification, repair, refactoring, and testing. Since the study describes it as a general-purpose assistant rather than emphasizing a single supported activity, code generation is the closest fit.

data.title: K-Search: LLM Kernel Generation via Co-Evolving Intrinsic World Model

form.note: K-Search is presented as a research system that plans and carries out iterative kernel optimization using an LLM world model and execution feedback, rather than as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: The system operates by iteratively expanding, updating, and pruning an explicit search tree, decoupling high-level planning from low-level code generation.

activity.note: The system generates concrete GPU kernel implementations from optimization intents and evaluates them; the paper emphasizes kernel generation and synthesis.
activity.evidence: We formulate GPU kernel synthesis as an optimization problem under a fixed evaluation budget.

data.title: NES: An Instruction-Free, Low-Latency Next Edit Suggestion Framework Powered by Learned Historical Editing Trajectories

form.note: NES is deployed as a directly used IDE-integrated solution, with suggestions accepted through Tab-key interaction.
form.evidence: captured exclusively via our IDE plugin

activity.note: NES supports changing existing code based on editing history and developer intent; code evolution is the closest fit for its code-editing function.
activity.evidence: NES-Edit Model analyzes the developer’s editing history, including refactoring patterns and API call sequences, to generate personalized and precise code modifications for the current edit.

data.title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery

form.note: MLEvolve is presented as a research framework of specialized agents for long-horizon algorithm discovery, not as a directly operated product.
form.evidence: an LLM-based self-evolving multi-agent framework for end-to-end machine learning algorithm discovery

activity.note: The framework generates code for candidate machine-learning solutions, with code generation identified as a core capability; iterative refinement is also supported.
activity.evidence: Base mode: Full code generation from scratch.

data.title: Zero-to-CAD: Agentic Synthesis of Interpretable CAD Programs at Million-Scale Without Real Data

form.note: Zero-to-CAD is presented as a research synthesis pipeline, with its main contribution being an integrated closed-loop approach rather than a directly operated product.
form.evidence: our contribution is integrating them into a robust closed-loop synthesis pipeline

activity.note: The pipeline generates new executable CAD construction code from part descriptions; code generation is its emphasized coding activity.
activity.evidence: The second stage takes each description from the catalog and generates executable CadQuery code that implements the described geometry.
